title: Expected counts are not a quota
intro: An original filled example showing how to use the seven record fields. Not a real learner record, experiment, answer key or official exam material.

fields.label: My conclusion
fields.value: For the stated Aa x Aa model, the probability of aa is 1/4. In 40 offspring, the expected aa count is 10; it is not a promise of exactly 10 in every batch.
fields.hint: State the prediction and its limits, not just a ratio.

fields.label: Evidence and source
fields.value: This is a constructed learning example, not an experiment. Both parents are Aa. The MedQGo Mendelian guide explains the gamete combinations. A fictional observed batch contains 12 AA, 17 Aa and 11 aa. These numbers are invented for comparison with the prediction.
fields.hint: Separate the given model, the reference and the invented observations.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: At this autosomal locus, each parent contributes A or a with probability 1/2; fertilisation is random. To compare predicted genotype proportions with surviving offspring, assume equal survival and reliable scoring. Complete dominance is needed for the phenotype grouping, not for the 1:2:1 genotype calculation.
fields.hint: Name the conditions your calculation uses.

fields.label: Reasoning or calculation
fields.value: The four ordered pairings are A+A, A+a, a+A and a+a, each with probability 1/4. The two middle pairings give Aa, so genotype probabilities are 1/4 AA, 1/2 Aa and 1/4 aa. Multiplying by 40 gives 10, 20 and 10 expected offspring. Under complete dominance, AA and Aa share the dominant phenotype: expected totals are 30 and 10. The invented observed totals are 12+17=29 dominant and 11 recessive.
fields.hint: Show the route from gametes to genotypes before grouping phenotypes.

fields.label: Limits and uncertainties
fields.value: The invented batch does not establish a biological result. An observed 11 aa instead of an expected 10 does not by itself disprove segregation or prove all assumptions. A statistical assessment would require an appropriate analysis. Dominant appearance alone cannot distinguish AA from Aa.
fields.hint: Do not turn a small discrepancy or an appearance into proof.

fields.label: What I changed
fields.value: Illustrative correction: I replaced “40 offspring must include 10 aa” with “10 is the expected aa count under this model; an individual batch can differ.” This is a model revision entry, not a report of an actual learner's mistake.
fields.hint: Explain why the old statement was too strong.

fields.label: Next review
fields.value: At my next study session, I will hide this sample and rebuild the four pairings. I will explain why Aa has two paths, state the dominance assumption, and separate expected counts from observed counts. I will choose a review date in my own record.
fields.hint: Specify something you will produce or explain; copying this record is not proof of understanding.
